items.followUp: Why do flowering plants produce spores by meiosis but form gametes by mitosis?

rubric.why: Meiosis in the diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores.
rubric.description: States that plants produce spores by meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking meiosis with spore production.

rubric.why: The haploid gametophyte forms gametes by mitosis.
rubric.description: States that plant gametes are formed by mitosis in the gametophyte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking mitosis with gamete formation.

modelAnswer: Plants show alternation of generations: the diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores by meiosis.
These spores grow into a haploid gametophyte, which produces gametes by mitosis.

items.followUp: Who discovered the role of ATP in muscle contraction, and who proposed its role in energy transfer in cells?

rubric.why: Karl Lohmann is credited with discovering ATP.
Lipmann described ATP as an energy-transfer molecule in the living cell.
rubric.description: Names the scientist who proposed ATP's energy-transfer role.

modelAnswer: ATP was discovered by Karl Lohmann in 1929.
Fritz Lipmann named ATP as an energy-transfer molecule in the living cell.

rubric.why: Oxidation is commonly described by electron loss, oxygen gain, or hydrogen loss.
rubric.description: Gives a correct definition or characteristic of oxidation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one accepted oxidation description.

rubric.why: Reduction is commonly described by electron gain, oxygen loss, or hydrogen gain.
rubric.description: Gives a correct definition or characteristic of reduction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one accepted reduction description.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the loss of electrons, addition of oxygen, or removal of hydrogen.
Reduction is the gain of electrons, removal of oxygen, or addition of hydrogen.

items.followUp: State the substrates and products of lipase and maltase.

rubric.why: Proteases digest proteins into smaller peptides and ultimately amino acids.
rubric.description: States the action of protease on proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying proteins as the substrate and amino acids as the end product.

rubric.why: Amylase breaks starch down into maltose.
rubric.description: States the action of amylase on starch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying starch as the substrate and maltose as the product.

modelAnswer: Protease breaks down proteins into peptides and ultimately amino acids.
Amylase breaks down starch into maltose.

items.followUp: Define trace minerals and name two examples.

rubric.why: Minerals are inorganic nutrients or elements needed by organisms.
rubric.description: Defines minerals as inorganic nutrients or elements required by organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, and magnesium are examples of major minerals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

modelAnswer: Minerals are inorganic elements required by organisms to perform various functions.
Two major minerals are calcium and phosphorus.

items.followUp: What is the function of the pulmonary artery?

rubric.why: The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart's left atrium.
rubric.description: States what blood the pulmonary vein carries and its route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying oxygenated blood travelling from the lungs to the left atrium.

rubric.why: Its function is to deliver oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
rubric.description: States the function of the pulmonary vein.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing delivery of oxygenated blood to the left atrium.

modelAnswer: The pulmonary vein is a blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.
Its function is to return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

items.followUp: Give two benefits of transpiration to a plant.

rubric.why: Transpiration can cause excessive water loss and wilting, so it is considered harmful.
rubric.description: Explains why transpiration is an evil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting harmful water loss or the risk of wilting.

rubric.why: Transpiration creates a pull that helps move water and minerals from roots to leaves.
rubric.description: Explains a necessary benefit of transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking transpiration with water/mineral transport or transpiration pull.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is an evil because excessive loss of water may cause a plant to wilt.
It is necessary because it creates a transpiration pull that helps transport water and minerals from roots to leaves.
It also helps cool the plant.

items.followUp: Explain how humidity, wind, and light affect the rate of transpiration.

rubric.why: Light generally causes stomata to open, increasing water-vapour loss.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of light on transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light increases transpiration, usually by opening stomata.

rubric.why: Higher temperature increases evaporation from leaf surfaces and raises transpiration.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature on transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that higher temperature increases the rate.

rubric.why: Humid air reduces the water-vapour gradient from leaf to air; dry air increases it.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of humidity on transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of high humidity or dry air.

rubric.why: Wind removes moist air near the leaf, while leaf area and leaf structures also affect water loss.
rubric.description: Explains one other factor affecting transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct effect of wind or a leaf feature.

modelAnswer: Light generally opens stomata and increases transpiration; darkness tends to reduce it.
Higher temperature increases evaporation and therefore increases transpiration.
High humidity reduces transpiration, while dry air increases it.
Wind increases transpiration by carrying away moist air around the leaf; a larger leaf area or more stomata also increases water loss, while a thick cuticle reduces it.
The availability of water in the soil also affects the rate: water shortage reduces transpiration.
